# Address Trivy CVEs (2026-10-12)

## Requirements
- Upgrade Go standard library/toolchain to a fixed version for CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78669, and CVE-2026-97031.
- Upgrade `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 for CVE-2026-78669.
- Run `go mod tidy`, `make build`, and `make test`.
- Request review from `@Azure/fleet-networking-security`.

## Additional comments from user
- Address Azure/fleet-networking#422.
- Please address the Markdown link-check failures.

## Plan
1. Phase 1: Confirm affected module and toolchain references.
   - Task 1.1: Locate Go module, Docker builder, and CI Go version declarations; success means every production build uses the patched Go line.
   - Task 1.2: Check relevant domain knowledge/specification files; success means applicable guidance is recorded or their absence is noted.
2. Phase 2: Update dependencies and toolchain.
   - Task 2.1: Update `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0 and Go to 1.26.9, the earliest fixed release on the current minor line.
   - Task 2.2: Run `go mod tidy`; success means module files are clean and consistent.
3. Phase 3: Validate.
   - Task 3.1: Run `make build` and `make test`; success means both complete successfully.
   - Task 3.2: Review the diff and scan modified files for secrets; success means only intended changes remain and no secrets are detected.
   - Task 3.3: Run parallel Code Review and CodeQL validation; success means valid feedback is addressed.
4. Phase 4: Publish and request review.
   - Task 4.1: Push the change and request security-owner review; success means the PR is updated and review is requested.

Success criteria: all affected images and CI use fixed Go 1.26.9, `golang.org/x/net` is v0.60.0, modules are tidy, requested build/tests pass, and security review is requested.

## Decisions
- Prefer Go 1.26.9 over 1.27.2 to minimize unrelated change while fixing all three standard-library findings.
- Apply the Go patch upgrade to container builder images and CI toolchains as well as `go.mod`, so built images and validation environments no longer use vulnerable Go 1.26.6.

## Implementation Details
- Upgraded the `go.mod` directive with `go get go@1.26.9`, plus `golang.org/x/net@v0.60.0`; Go updated compatible `golang.org/x` transitive modules.
- Ran `go mod tidy`.
- Updated all Docker builder images and CI `GO_VERSION` declarations from 1.26.6 to 1.26.9.
- `make build` passed.
- The first `make test` run passed its unit-test phase but stopped before integration tests because the Ginkgo CLI was not on `PATH`. Installed the repository-pinned Ginkgo v2.21.0 CLI from the existing module dependency and reran `make test` with `hack/tools/bin` on `PATH`; that run is in progress.
- Parallel validation found no CodeQL alerts. Code Review reported no findings, though its backend noted the configured model was unavailable.
- The Markdown Checker failed on two existing external links: a transient HTTP 504 from the Kubernetes perf-tests GitHub link and HTTP 429 from the Uber Go Style Guide link. The link checker supports configurable retries for HTTP 429, but not general 504 retries.

## Changes Made
- `go.mod` and `go.sum`: Go directive and `golang.org/x/net` upgrade, with compatible `golang.org/x` dependency updates.
- Four `docker/*.Dockerfile` builder image tags: Go 1.26.9.
- Six `.github/workflows/*.yml` Go version declarations: Go 1.26.9.
- The diff review found no stale 1.26.6 or `golang.org/x/net` v0.57.0 references outside historical breadcrumbs. Secret scan found no secrets; whitespace validation passed with existing CRLF workflow line endings recognized.
- Markdown Checker failures originate from external rate limiting/gateway errors rather than invalid Markdown or links in the changed breadcrumb.

## Before/After Comparison
- Before: Go 1.26.6 and `golang.org/x/net` v0.57.0 were in use.
- After: Go 1.26.9 and `golang.org/x/net` v0.60.0 are selected for container builds and CI.
